title: Isolated VPC deployment: connectivity, offline upgrade flow and deployment acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Overview:
This ticket captures the requirements and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC deployments that run in fully isolated or air-gapped networks and for upgrade workflows that must work without direct internet access. The goal is to define clear, testable criteria for networking configuration, artifact delivery, upgrade orchestration (online and offline), security controls (KMS, signing, RBAC, audit trails), and observability constraints so we can ship a reliable private deployment experience for regulated customers.

Background and motivation:
Several enterprise customers require private VPC or on-prem deployments with strict egress controls and long maintenance windows. Historically upgrades assumed connectivity to our artifact registry and telemetry endpoints; this proposal documents two supported upgrade modes (online and offline) and the precise networking and operational requirements for each.

Goals:
- Support fully air-gapped installs and upgrades via signed offline bundles.
- Define preflight checks and automated validations to unblock upgrades safely.
- Ensure auditability: upgrade events are recorded in local logs and exported to customer SIEM if configured.
- Keep operational handoff minimal: operator-run and self-serve upgrade modes with clear runbook.

Non-goals:
- We will not ship a managed artifact mirror service for customers in this release. Customers must provide an internal mirror or use our signed bundle process.
- No support for Windows worker nodes in this release (Linux only).

Assumptions:
- Customers can provide a bastion or jump host for artifact transfer when fully air-gapped.
- Cluster time sync (NTP) is already configured.
- Customer will expose at least a private DNS resolver for cluster domain lookups, or configure /etc/hosts entries as documented.

Decisions and trade-offs:
- We will require signed upgrade bundles (container images optionally pre-pulled) instead of building an internal mirror to reduce operational burden.
- Preference given to rolling, orchestrated upgrades with optional maintenance mode; fully offline forced reboots permitted only when rollback automation is available.

Artifacts and references:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Isolated+VPC+Upgrade+PRD
- GH proposal: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/467
- Runbook draft: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/private-deploy/upgrade-offline
acceptance_criteria: Preflight validation: 'redwood preflight' or equivalent returns success when run in-customer environment with the required permissions and network rules in place.
Offline bundle integrity: provided offline upgrade bundle must include a signed manifest and checksums; installer verifies signatures and refuses unsigned bundles.
No external egress required for air-gapped upgrade: full upgrade completes end-to-end without outbound internet access when using the offline bundle and documented transfer mechanisms.
Controlled maintenance mode: API route /admin/maintenance toggles maintenance state; during maintenance, client traffic receives 503 and backlog queue drains according to configured settings.
Rolling upgrade safety: control-plane and worker nodes upgraded in sequence per chart; during upgrade core APIs remain available with degraded capacity but no data corruption.
Rollback test: a simulated failed upgrade is reversible using the documented rollback command within the maintenance window and restores previous API and model-serving state.

Certificate and KMS handling: CA and TLS cert rotation is supported via customer KMS; if KMS is not available, operator must be able to supply certs via the bundle and rotation post-upgrade is documented.
Audit logs: upgrade start/finish events, operator identity, and bundle checksums are recorded to local audit logs and can be exported to customer SIEM (if configured).
Telemetry constraints: components default to local metrics retention; a telemetry relay option (pull-based) is available and documented for customers who permit egress through a proxy.

Resource validation: post-upgrade health checks pass (API /health, GPU node readiness, KV cache sanity) and tokenized performance smoke tests show no regression beyond +10% latency of the pre-upgrade baseline.
Upgrade bundle size: documented maximum offline bundle size is enforced by the installer (default 50GB), and installer fails fast if bundle is truncated or corrupted.

Operator documentation: runbook includes step-by-step offline transfer, checksum verification, dry-run option, and post-upgrade validation checklist; at least one customer has completed a dry-run end-to-end during validation phase.
validation_steps: Stage an isolated test environment that mirrors customer egress policies (no outbound to artifact registry or telemetry endpoints).
Generate a signed offline bundle using the internal tooling and copy it into the isolated environment via a bastion host or physical media.
Run preflight checks and record output; verify that missing permissions/network rules fail preflight with actionable messages.
Execute offline upgrade in a short maintenance window; monitor logs and capture timestamps for start/end, and verify audit events contain operator identity and bundle checksum.
Induce a controlled failure mid-upgrade to validate rollback path; ensure system returns to healthy state and no data loss observed.
Measure API latency and throughput before and after upgrade using the tokenized smoke tests; ensure regression tolerance is within acceptance criteria.
Verify certificate handling: confirm KMS-based rotation or manual cert injection method works and TLS sessions remain valid after rotation.
Confirm local metrics and logs are available post-upgrade and that telemetry relay can be configured by customer to export metrics if they open a proxy path.
Document lessons learned and update runbook and preflight messages based on operator feedback.
Obtain sign-off from Security, Eng, and Solutions Engineering that checklist items are satisfied for staged customer flows.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Bundle corruption during transfer. Mitigation: Strong checksums, manifest signing, and installer verifies integrity before any state changes.
Risk: Customer misconfiguration of network rules causing incomplete upgrade. Mitigation: Clear preflight checks with explicit actionable messages and a dry-run mode.
Risk: Long downtime for large clusters. Mitigation: Support staggered rolling upgrades and recommend performance-based batch sizes; provide estimated duration calculator in runbook.

Risk: Incomplete observability when egress is blocked. Mitigation: Provide local retention defaults and a telemetry relay that can be run inside customer network and polled by our Ops only when authorized.
Risk: Key compromise in bundle signing process. Mitigation: Use short-lived signing keys, rotate internal keys, and publish verification tooling for offline use.
open_questions: Should we support a customer-managed OCI registry mirror workflow in this release or defer to Q3?
Do we require customers to run our telemetry relay, or can we accept a best-effort local-only observability baseline for sign-off?
What is the exact maximum allowed bundle size we can reasonably support for customers with limited transfer bandwidth? (proposal: 50GB default)
Is there appetite to require a dedicated upgrade bastion image (thin agent) shipped by Redwood to simplify air-gap transfers?
How will licensing checks be enforced offline (entitlement file vs. online license check)? Current plan: entitlement file signed and included in bundle.
